problem_statement: The nightly high-value release run crashed again at 02:14 with `PolicyTimeout: fraud policy service timed out for order HV-88213`. The exception escapes `run_release_queue`, so every order after the one that timed out stays unprocessed until someone reruns the job by hand. The fraud policy service has short latency spikes a few times a week and we can't keep paging on-call for them. Please make the release run handle a policy-service timeout for a single order and finish cleanly, processing the rest of the queue.

Our nightly high-value release run fell over again at 02:14, this time with `PolicyTimeout: fraud policy service timed out for order HV-88213`. Because the exception propagates out of `run_release_queue`, all orders queued after the timed-out one are left unprocessed until somebody manually reruns the job. The fraud policy service sees brief latency spikes a few times each week, and paging on-call every time isn't sustainable. Please change the release run so that a policy-service timeout on a single order is handled and the run completes cleanly, still processing the remainder of the queue.

At 02:14 the nightly high-value release run crashed once more, failing with `PolicyTimeout: fraud policy service timed out for order HV-88213`. That exception isn't caught inside `run_release_queue`, so it escapes and every subsequent order in the queue remains unprocessed until the job is rerun by hand. Short latency spikes on the fraud policy service happen a few times a week, and we can't continue paging on-call over them. Requested: have the release run handle a policy-service timeout for one order and finish cleanly, working through the rest of the queue.
